page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a 16 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. This virtual machine is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 640 GB NVMe SSD.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 10 percent, and the Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, falls within the average tier. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 86.9 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 60.95 GB/sec for writes. However, the system exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, static web serving throughput, and database operations, which rank in the bottom 25 percent. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, with medium-model prompt processing falling into the bottom 10 percent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high memory density of 8 GB per vCPU alongside dedicated CPU resources and a substantial local NVMe SSD, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extreme multi-threaded compute. The hardware profile is well-suited for memory-cached applications, text processing, software compilation, and moderate general-purpose workloads. It is less optimal for high-throughput static web serving or intensive database operations due to lower benchmark results in those specific areas.
